mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This relationship holds continuously across the rate spectrum without threshold activation.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS against 60-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX 60-day returns is negative in more than 50% of 1-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points over the past month signals an imminent economic slowdown, prompting risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 60% or more of the instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns, or the Rank IC for the trigger condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a misallocation of consumer spending towards durable goods at the expense of services, triggering a market correction and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises and RSAFS falls in 1 month
failure_condition: In 60% or more of the instances where HOUST rises and RSAFS falls in 1 month, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns, or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high industrial growth regime (INDPRO > 110), a monthly decline in industrial production exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals an imminent economic deceleration, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the high industrial growth regime (INDPRO > 110), 60% or more of the instances where INDPRO falls > 0.5pp in 1 month are followed by positive 20-day SPX returns, or the Rank IC for the signal within the regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand for housing, which correlates with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for HOUST against 5-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between HOUST and SPX 5-day returns is negative in more than 50% of 1-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index value exceeding 260 (indicating elevated inflation) triggers a market reaction to anticipated monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 60% or more of the instances where CPIAUCSL > 260, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns, or the Rank IC for the trigger condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 50k increase) and declining unemployment rate (UNRATE > 0.1pp decrease) in the past month signals an overheating labor market, prompting fears of inflation and monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 50k and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: In 60% or more of the instances where PAYEMS rises > 50k and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns, or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth rate > 2% annualized), a monthly decline in retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 1% signals a weakening consumer sector, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth rate > 2% annualized), 60% or more of the instances where RSAFS falls > 1% in 1 month are followed by positive 60-day SPX returns, or the Rank IC for the signal within the regime is below 0.03.
